---
title: "Topology Checker"
date: 2026-09-03
categories: [tool, geometry]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and check it for the five recurring topology errors — overlap, gap, sliver, duplicates, dangle. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether any
feature overlaps, leaves a gap, is a sliver, duplicates another, or
(for lines) dangles unconnected.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

This is diagnosis only, not repair — fixing a topology error almost
always requires a human decision (see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for why), so there's no
"Fix" step here, just the report and a map to inspect it on.

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using GeoPandas/Shapely underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/topology-errors.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained one check at a time.

Gap and sliver aren't absolute properties of a dataset — they depend
on a judgment call. **Sliver threshold** (compactness, 0-1): how thin
counts as "not a real shape" — lower catches only thinner slivers.
**Gap search distance** (degrees): how close two features need to be
before a gap between them counts — larger finds gaps further apart.

*First run loads the Python engine — expect 30-40 seconds. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

```{.webgeods-python #topology-diagnose-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
#| inject: [sliverThreshold, gapProximity]
import math
from shapely.geometry import mapping

def geom_family(gdf):
    types = set(gdf.geometry.geom_type)
    if types <= {"Polygon", "MultiPolygon"}:
        return "polygon"
    if types <= {"LineString", "MultiLineString"}:
        return "line"
    if types <= {"Point", "MultiPoint"}:
        return "point"
    return "mixed"

def check_overlap(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                area = gi.intersection(gj).area
                results[i].append(("overlap", j, area))
                results[j].append(("overlap", i, area))
    return results

def check_duplicate(gdf):
    n = len(gdf)
    results = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if gdf.geometry.iloc[i].equals(gdf.geometry.iloc[j]):
                results[i].append(("duplicate", j, 0))
                results[j].append(("duplicate", i, 0))
    return results

def check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=0.15):
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        perim = geom.length
        area = geom.area
        if perim > 0:
            compactness = 4 * math.pi * area / (perim ** 2)
            if compactness < compactness_threshold:
                results[i].append(("sliver", None, compactness))
    return results

def check_gap(gdf, min_area=1e-6, proximity=0.06):
    n = len(gdf)
    gaps = []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            gi, gj = gdf.geometry.iloc[i], gdf.geometry.iloc[j]
            if gi.overlaps(gj):
                continue
            if gi.equals(gj):
                continue
            if gi.distance(gj) > proximity:
                continue
            pair_union = gi.union(gj)
            gap_geom = pair_union.convex_hull.difference(pair_union)
            if not gap_geom.is_empty:
                parts = gap_geom.geoms if hasattr(gap_geom, "geoms") else [gap_geom]
                for part in parts:
                    if part.area > min_area:
                        gaps.append(part)
    return gaps

def check_dangle(gdf, tolerance=1e-9):
    endpoints = []
    for i, geom in enumerate(gdf.geometry):
        coords = list(geom.coords)
        endpoints.append((i, "start", coords[0]))
        endpoints.append((i, "end", coords[-1]))
    results = [[] for _ in range(len(gdf))]
    for i, which, (x, y) in endpoints:
        connected = False
        for j, which2, (x2, y2) in endpoints:
            if j == i:
                continue
            if ((x - x2) ** 2 + (y - y2) ** 2) ** 0.5 <= tolerance:
                connected = True
                break
        if not connected:
            results[i].append(("dangle", which, 0))
    return results

def detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=0.15, gap_proximity=0.06):
    family = geom_family(gdf)
    n = len(gdf)
    per_feature = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    extra_features = []

    dup = check_duplicate(gdf)
    for i in range(n):
        per_feature[i].extend(dup[i])

    if family == "polygon":
        ov = check_overlap(gdf)
        sl = check_sliver(gdf, compactness_threshold=sliver_threshold)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(ov[i])
            per_feature[i].extend(sl[i])
        for gap_geom in check_gap(gdf, proximity=gap_proximity):
            extra_features.append({
                "type": "Feature",
                "properties": {
                    "name": "gap", "error_type": "gap", "has_error": True,
                    "partner": "", "metric": round(gap_geom.area, 6), "severity": "warning"
                },
                "geometry": mapping(gap_geom)
            })
    elif family == "line":
        dg = check_dangle(gdf)
        for i in range(n):
            per_feature[i].extend(dg[i])

    # Report columns computed here, then assigned onto gdf itself
    # instead of building each feature's properties dict from scratch
    # (an earlier version did that, discarding every other original
    # column the uploaded file had — a real difference from
    # geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd, which has always preserved
    # them). "name" is guaranteed present by the caller already.
    names = gdf["name"]
    error_types, has_errors, partners, metrics, severities = [], [], [], [], []
    for i in range(n):
        errs = per_feature[i]
        has_error = len(errs) > 0
        partner_idx = errs[0][1] if has_error and isinstance(errs[0][1], int) else None
        error_types.append(errs[0][0] if has_error else "")
        has_errors.append(has_error)
        partners.append(str(names.iloc[partner_idx]) if partner_idx is not None else "")
        metrics.append(round(errs[0][2], 6) if has_error else 0)
        severities.append("error" if has_error else "")

    gdf["error_type"] = error_types
    gdf["has_error"] = has_errors
    gdf["partner"] = partners
    gdf["metric"] = metrics
    gdf["severity"] = severities

    # Same reasoning as geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd: a None in an
    # ORIGINAL column (not under our control) would otherwise vanish
    # silently crossing the Pyodide->JS bridge as a live cell value.
    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

    # Kept as two separate collections instead of one concatenated
    # list (an earlier version merged them): a gap is synthetic — it
    # has no corresponding row in the uploaded file — and merging it
    # in inflated the feature count on a dense test file to 54 rows
    # for 10 real features (44 pairwise "gap" candidates), with no way
    # for the map to show just the original data or for the count to
    # distinguish "real feature" from "synthetic gap". JS puts each
    # collection on its own map source (topology-py / topology-gaps-py)
    # instead. Gaps stay a fixed, small property set (unlike the real
    # features above) — a gap has no original row to inherit columns
    # from, it's purely computed.
    return {
        "features": gdf.__geo_interface__,
        "gaps": {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": extra_features}
    }

import geopandas as gpd

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

# The sliver/gap thresholds above (and every check_*() function) work
# in gdf's OWN coordinate units — "Gap search distance (degrees)" in
# the panel only means what it says if gdf is actually in a geographic
# CRS — so it's reprojected to WGS84 here before any check runs, not
# just before the map draws it.
crs_warning = None
original_crs = None
if gdf is not None:
    if gdf.crs is None:
        gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
        crs_warning = "No CRS found in the uploaded file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
    original_crs = gdf.crs
    if original_crs != "EPSG:4326":
        gdf = gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

def export_crs(g):
    # Reprojects `g` back to the CRS it was uploaded in — used by the
    # download button below, so what comes out matches what went in
    # even though the checks above always run in WGS84.
    if g is None or original_crs is None or original_crs == "EPSG:4326":
        return g
    return g.to_crs(original_crs)

# No built-in fallback anymore (an earlier version diagnosed two
# hardcoded example polygons automatically whenever nothing had been
# uploaded) — see geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's identical change:
# the page now starts genuinely empty until the user either uploads a
# file or clicks "Load example" below, so "no results yet" actually
# means no results yet.
EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}
if gdf is not None:
    result = detect_and_check(gdf, sliver_threshold=sliverThreshold, gap_proximity=gapProximity)
    result["originalCrsFeatures"] = export_crs(gdf).__geo_interface__
    result["crsWarning"] = crs_warning
else:
    result = {"features": EMPTY_FC, "gaps": EMPTY_FC, "originalCrsFeatures": EMPTY_FC, "crsWarning": None}
result
```

runCheck = async () => {
  window.sliverThreshold = +document.getElementById("sliver-threshold-control").value;
  window.gapProximity = +document.getElementById("gap-proximity-control").value;

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// The color is decided by JS, not Python — see topology-errors.qmd for
// the full explanation. The geometry type isn't fixed (polygons for
// overlap/gap/sliver/duplicates, lines for dangle), so the paint
// itself depends on the data: setGeoJSON() (shared/map.js) detects on
// its own when the layer's TYPE needs to change and recreates it.
errorPaint = (data) => {
  const geometryType = data?.features?.find((f) => f?.geometry?.type)?.geometry?.type ?? "";
  const colorExpr = ["case", ["==", ["get", "has_error"], true], "#e05252", "#3d5a73"];
  if (geometryType === "LineString" || geometryType === "MultiLineString") {
    return { "line-color": colorExpr, "line-width": 4 };
  }
  if (geometryType === "Point" || geometryType === "MultiPoint") {
    return { "circle-color": colorExpr, "circle-radius": 6 };
  }
  return { "fill-color": colorExpr, "fill-opacity": 0.55 };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Gaps are always polygons (check_gap() builds them from a
// convex-hull difference) — no per-geometry-type branching needed,
// unlike errorPaint above. --attenzione/warning amber, matching the
// "severity": "warning" Python already tags every gap feature with
// (as opposed to "error" for a real per-feature problem) — same
// color language, not an arbitrary second color.
gapPaint = ({
  "fill-color": "#c48a2e",
  "fill-opacity": 0.45
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
pyErrors = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("topology-diagnose-py", Generators)
{
  if (pyErrors) {
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("topology-py", pyErrors.features, { paint: errorPaint(pyErrors.features) });
    // Gaps live on their own source so the map can show just the
    // real data (features) or both at once (features + gaps in
    // amber) — visibility follows topologyView, the same tab state
    // the table below uses, so switching tabs and re-running Check
    // both keep the map and the table in sync with each other.
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("topology-gaps-py", pyErrors.gaps, {
      paint: gapPaint,
      layout: { visibility: topologyView === "gaps" ? "visible" : "none" }
    });
    // Zooms to the real data's bounds regardless of which tab is
    // active — same as geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's pyDiagnose
    // effect — so switching tabs never itself moves the map. A no-op
    // on an empty FeatureCollection.
    await sharedMap.fitToData(pyErrors.features);
    mutable exportFeatures = pyErrors.originalCrsFeatures;
    mutable crsWarning = pyErrors.crsWarning;
  }
}
```

// Two independent, stable tableCell()s (never re-created — only
// their .style.display is toggled by tabbedResultsView below) instead
// of one table whose sourceIds swaps reactively with topologyView:
// each keeps its own tableCell()-internal "sourcedata" subscription
// alive and correctly reacting to ITS OWN source's data changes the
// entire time, with no risk of losing or double-registering a
// listener across a tab switch.
featuresTableCell = sharedMap.tableCell(["topology-py"], null, Generators, {
  rowClassName: (row) => row.has_error === "true" ? "webgeods-row-invalid" : "",
  emptyMessage: "No results yet"
})

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Tab bar + both panes in one cell (output:false-free, physically
// positioned here where the table should display — same "avoid the
// scatter-on-load bug" reasoning as every button on this page, just
// for a single auto-displayed cell instead of one moved via
// controlPanelRow). Reactive on topologyView, but only ever
// recreates this thin wrapper + tab buttons — featuresTableCell/
// gapsTableCell above are NEVER re-created, only shown/hidden, so
// their own reactivity (and any current row selection) survives a
// tab switch untouched.
tabbedResultsView = {
  const tab = (key, label) => {
    const button = document.createElement("button");
    button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
    if (topologyView !== key) button.dataset.variant = "outline";
    button.textContent = label;
    button.onclick = () => { mutable topologyView = key; };
    return button;
  };

  const tabs = document.createElement("div");
  tabs.className = "webgeods-panel-row";
  tabs.append(tab("features", "Original geometries"), tab("gaps", "Gaps"));

  featuresTableCell.style.display = topologyView === "features" ? "" : "none";
  gapsTableCell.style.display = topologyView === "gaps" ? "" : "none";

  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.append(tabs, featuresTableCell, gapsTableCell);
  return wrap;
}

// total/errors count ONLY the real uploaded features (topology-py) —
// gaps are synthetic and get their own count instead of inflating
// this one, see pyErrors's comment.
topologyStats = Generators.observe((change) => {
  const compute = () => {
    const features = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("topology-py")?.features ?? [];
    const gaps = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("topology-gaps-py")?.features ?? [];
    const total = features.length;
    const errors = features.filter((f) => f.properties?.has_error === true).length;
    change({ total, errors, gaps: gaps.length });
  };
  compute();
  const handler = (e) => {
    if (
      e.dataType === "source" &&
      e.sourceDataType === "content" &&
      (e.sourceId === "topology-py" || e.sourceId === "topology-gaps-py")
    ) {
      compute();
    }
  };
  sharedMap.map.on("sourcedata", handler);
  return () => sharedMap.map.off("sourcedata", handler);
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
resetChecker = async () => {
  const empty = { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [] };
  if (sharedMap.getGeoJSON("topology-py")) {
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("topology-py", empty);
  }
  if (sharedMap.getGeoJSON("topology-gaps-py")) {
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("topology-gaps-py", empty);
  }
  mutable exportFeatures = null;
  mutable crsWarning = null;
}
```

  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.dataset.variant = "outline";
  button.textContent = "🔄 Reset";
  button.onclick = () => resetChecker();

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// WebGeoDS.downloadBlob (shared/download.js) — this page used to have
// its own near-duplicate of geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's own
// function; that page's comment named "a second tool duplicating
// this" as the trigger for promoting it, which is exactly what
// happened, so it's shared now instead of duplicated a third time.
downloadButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.dataset.variant = "outline";
  button.textContent = "⬇ Download";
  button.onclick = () => {
    const base = WebGeoDS.Upload.baseName(uploadedFiles);
    // Original features only, same set as the Features tab/topology-py
    // — a gap has no corresponding row in the uploaded file (that's
    // the whole reason it got its own map source and table tab
    // instead of being merged in), so a downloaded "here's your data
    // plus its topology report" file shouldn't reintroduce synthetic
    // rows the source data never had either. exportFeatures (not the
    // map source) so the download comes back in the file's own CRS,
    // not the WGS84 working copy the checks/map use — see
    // topology-diagnose-py's export_crs().
    const data = exportFeatures ?? { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [] };
    WebGeoDS.downloadBlob(
      JSON.stringify(data, null, 2),
      base ? `${base}-topology-report.geojson` : "topology-report.geojson",
      "application/geo+json",
      { tool: "topology-checker" }
    );
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// output:false: this cell's own definition sits well before the
// panel in the document — without it, the fully-grouped row would
// flash into view there FIRST (Quarto's own auto-display), then
// disappear and reappear down in the panel once ${controlPanelRow}
// mounts the same node — same reasoning as every button cell above.
//
// One DOM node grouping the upload control + Load example/Check/
// Download/Reset + the live status, built in JS rather than composed
// with several `${...}` markdown interpolations side by side —
// Pandoc's math-dollar parser reads adjacent `${x} ${y}` in the same
// paragraph as inline math and swallows them, and even `${x}`/`${y}`
// on separate paragraphs has its own problem (see uploadControl's
// comment above). A single `${controlPanelRow}` avoids both.
controlPanelRow = {
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.className = "webgeods-panel-row";
  row.append(uploadControl, loadExampleButton, checkButton, downloadButton, resetMapButton);
  const status = document.createElement("span");
  status.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
  // "with an error" counts real features only (never gaps — see
  // topologyStats' own comment); "total gaps" is the separate count
  // of synthetic gap features found between them, so the two numbers
  // together can't be misread as "N of these M things are broken"
  // when M actually mixes two different kinds of thing.
  const base = `${topologyStats.total} feature, ${topologyStats.errors} with an error, ${topologyStats.gaps} total gaps`;
  // crsWarning referenced here (not just read elsewhere) so this cell
  // is reactive on it — only known once Check has actually run, after
  // this row was first built.
  status.textContent = crsWarning ? `${base} — ⚠️ ${crsWarning}` : base;
  row.appendChild(status);
  return row;
}
```
